prompt:
You are an associate analyst at Marshfield Croft Partners in the Equity Capital Markets group. Your managing director, Rashida Holm, has assigned you to build a DCF model for IPO pricing analysis of NVIDIA Corporation, based on the company's most recent ARS filing dated May 12, 2026.

Rashida wants a fully functional Excel workbook that an equity syndicate desk could use to anchor price talk on a hypothetical NVIDIA IPO. The model needs to be presentation-ready — clean formatting, consistent units, no circular references, print areas set. She'll be reviewing this directly, so everything should be clearly labeled and auditable.

Build the model using the following structure and requirements:

- Five tabs: Assumptions, Income Statement, DCF, Valuation, and Sensitivity. Hardcode all base-case historical financials in the Assumptions tab, separate from any projected line items.
- Base period is NVIDIA's FY2026 (fiscal year ending January 25, 2026). Key inputs: revenues of $215,938M, gross profit of $153,463M, operating income of $130,387M, net income of $120,067M, R&D expense of $18,497M, SG&A of $4,579M, diluted EPS of $4.90/share, and cash and equivalents of $10,605M.
- Project at least 5 years of unlevered free cash flows from the FY2026 base. The projection must walk through NOPAT, then add back D&A, subtract capex, and adjust for changes in working capital to arrive at UFCF — do not shortcut from net income. Use R&D and SG&A as the basis for projecting opex; treat R&D as an expense, not capex.
- Revenue growth, margin, and capex assumptions must be explicitly stated and defensible for a large-cap US semiconductor name. All dollar figures in consistent units (millions or billions) with column headers stating the unit.
- Derive WACC using CAPM for cost of equity. NVIDIA's balance sheet shows total assets of $206,803M, total liabilities of $49,510M, and stockholders' equity of $157,293M — use this capital structure to weight the components. Beta, equity risk premium, and risk-free rate assumptions should fall within market-consensus ranges for large-cap semis.
- Calculate terminal value using both a perpetuity growth method and an exit multiple method, each with clearly stated assumptions.
- Reconcile enterprise value to equity value per share: subtract net debt (liabilities less cash), divide by implied share count, and cross-reference against the $4.90 diluted EPS as a sanity check.
- Sensitivity tab: matrix of implied equity value per share across varying WACC and terminal growth rate assumptions. Include at least one public comparable or transaction multiple as a cross-check on the DCF output.
- Since this is IPO pricing work, include a simple proceeds waterfall showing dilution at various offer price scenarios.

explicit_requirements: Build a fully functional DCF model in Excel that outputs an implied IPO price range for NVIDIA Corporation.
Use the latest annual financials from the 2026-01-25 fiscal year-end as the base case historical inputs (revenues $215.9B, gross profit $153.5B, operating income $130.4B, net income $120.1B).
Project at least 5 years of unlevered free cash flows starting from the FY2026 base period, with explicit revenue growth, margin, and capex assumptions.
Calculate a terminal value using both a perpetuity growth method and an exit multiple method, with clearly stated assumptions for each.

Discount projected cash flows using a WACC framework that derives the cost of equity via CAPM and incorporates NVIDIA's actual capital structure from the balance sheet (total assets $206.8B, liabilities $49.5B, equity $157.3B).
Include a sensitivity analysis tab showing implied equity value per share across a matrix of WACC and terminal growth rate assumptions.
Reference diluted EPS of $4.90/share and cash and equivalents of $10.6B to reconcile to per-share equity value.
Clearly label all source assumptions and hardcode pinned financials separately from projected line items so the model is auditable.

Use NVIDIA's R&D expense ($18.5B) and SG&A ($4.6B) as the basis for projecting operating expenses; do not treat R&D as capex unless explicitly justified.
The model must be presentation-ready for a senior MD review: clean formatting, print areas set, no circular references unless intentionally flagged.

- Revenue growth assumption of 4.0% (sector-typical for tech_semis)
